name: Herod Agrippa I
facts: Grandson of Herod the Great; not the Herod of Jesus’ birth.
Executed the apostle James and imprisoned Peter earlier in this chapter (12:1–3).
Josephus also records his sudden death at Caesarea in AD 44 (Antiquities 19.8.2).

name: Herod the Great
facts: Ruled when Jesus was born.
Rebuilt the Jerusalem temple.
Father of Herod Antipas and grandfather of Agrippa I.

name: Tyre
facts: Wealthy coastal trading city north of Galilee.
Depended on Galilean and Judean grain and food (Acts 12:20).

name: Sidon
summary: Phoenician port city, north of Tyre
facts: Paired with Tyre in the Bible as neighboring coastal cities.

name: Blastus
facts: Mentioned only here in the Bible.
Official in charge of the king’s bedchamber, so he had the king’s ear.

name: Angel of the Lord
facts: Same phrase used for Peter’s rescue earlier in Acts 12 (12:7).
In 12:23 the angel brings judgment rather than deliverance.

name: Barnabas
facts: Name means “son of encouragement.”
Traveling companion of Saul on the first missionary journey.
Cousin of John Mark (Colossians 4:10).

name: Saul (Paul)
facts: Jewish name Saul; Roman name Paul, used from Acts 13:9.
Had come to Jerusalem with Barnabas to bring famine relief (Acts 11:30).

name: Jerusalem
summary: Capital of Judea and center of the early church
facts: Home base of the apostles in Acts.
Site of Herod’s persecution in Acts 12.

name: John Mark
facts: Traditionally the author of the Gospel of Mark.
His mother Mary hosted the church prayer meeting (12:12).
Left the mission, later restored (Acts 15:37–39; 2 Timothy 4:11).

name: Peter
summary: Apostle; leader of the Jerusalem church
facts: Also called Simon and Cephas.
Imprisoned by Herod Agrippa I and freed by an angel (Acts 12:3–11).

name: Caesarea
summary: Roman port and provincial capital on the Mediterranean coast
facts: Built by Herod the Great and named for Caesar Augustus.
Where Agrippa I died in AD 44 (Acts 12:19–23).
